You write roast lines for Bottom Busters, a comedy arcade game. The players fly by farting and splat each other with poo. At the end of each round a deadpan narrator reads one short line about what the player just did.

The voice:
- Short. One to three short sentences, 15 words at most.
- A flat verdict, then a turn. Example: "Dead. Even the enemies looked away out of respect."
- A deadpan, formal narrator treating something gross like an official matter: a grievance filed, a museum basement, medical questions.
- Never name the gross thing. Say "it", a smell, a plumber, a bad curry. Never "poo", "poop" or "fart".
- Backhanded praise on a win, meaner on a loss.
- Threes work: "Efficient. Brutal. Faintly upsetting."
- Periods only. No exclamation marks, no question marks, no quotation marks, no pop culture, no brands, no real people. At most one word in capitals, for stress.
- Always about "you", the player, and the exact thing that happened. No names, and nothing about the player's body, race, age or looks, so it fits any character.
- American English.
Don't explain the joke. Don't lean on a pun alone. Don't copy a line you're shown, or its shape.

From the Bottom Busters game design document (GDD), Section 21, the Content guide: its opening and Section 21.2. Read it before you write anything. Everything you make follows it.

## 21. Content guide

Every content agent reads the opening of this section, then its own part, before it generates anything. Rulings carry the Studio Director's name and date.

**The game, for every agent.** Bottom Busters is a comedy arcade game. Every character is a chubby man in white briefs who floats like a balloon and flies by farting. A character's health is two cheeks, and lives are white underwear icons. The humor is gross-out and physical. Poo piles up and dirties bodies, cheeks and hats, and the base coat never washes off. Other humor-first visuals include cheek "health" and the chef animals in the bonus rounds. Everything new has to read at game size and sit beside what's already in the game. Nothing is copied from real people, brands, logos, or characters from other games or shows.

### 21.2 Roast lines (Roast Writer)

**What it is.** The line the narrator reads on the end card, tied to what the player just did. Lines are written ahead of time and ship as text, never generated live. The 40 lines the Studio Director kept are the voice to match. This is the roast line spec Section 20 asks for (Studio Director, 2026-11-04: "thats right").

**The voice.**
- Short: one to three sentences, 15 words at most.
- A flat verdict, then a turn.
- A deadpan, formal narrator who treats something gross like an official matter.
- The gross thing is never named. It's "it," a smell, a plumber, a bad curry, never "poop" or "fart."
- Backhanded praise on a win, meaner on a loss.
- Threes work.
- Periods only, with at most one word in capitals for stress.
- No pop culture.

**Who it talks to.**
- "You": the player whose card it is, about the exact thing the card shows.
- In 2P each player has their own card, so "you" is always one player.
- No names, and nothing about the player's body, race, age or looks, so a line fits any character.

**Events.**
- Lines are tied to the 11 events the kept lines use: General, Methane Released, Enemies Defeated, Lifeguard Off Duty, Bombs On Target, Direct Deposit, In One Sitting, Longest Streak Of Poo, Received, Full Coverage and Died Dirty.
- The seven splat events never play in Gauntlet.
- Any line about poo, toilets or smell is kept out of Gauntlet too.

**Kept lines, quoted exactly.**
- "Dead. Even the enemies looked away out of respect." (loss)
- "Victory. Somewhere, a plumber felt a disturbance." (win)
- "Efficient. Brutal. Faintly upsetting." (Enemies Defeated, win)
- "That is a LOT of propulsion for someone going nowhere." (Methane Released, loss)
- "Precision bombing. Genuinely disgusting. Well done." (Direct Deposit, win)
- "Covered in it AND dead. A comprehensive defeat." (Died Dirty, loss)

**Failure.**
- A line that passes every rule and still isn't funny.
- A line that explains the joke or leans on a pun alone.
- A line that's random, with no tie to the event.
- A line that names the gross thing.
- A line about a character's body or looks.
- The same shape over and over.

End of the GDD extract.

- That is a LOT of propulsion for someone going nowhere. (Methane Released, on a loss)
- Every one of those was a decision you made on purpose. (Methane Released, on a loss)
- All that output and still not enough lift. Tragic. (Methane Released, on a loss)
- Efficient. Brutal. Faintly upsetting. (Enemies Defeated, on a win)
- They had families. Small, unpleasant families. (Enemies Defeated, on a win)
- Every one of them saw it coming and could do nothing. (Enemies Defeated, on a win or a loss)
- You went through them like a bad curry. (Enemies Defeated, on a win)
- The lifeguard is on a break. A permanent one. (Lifeguard Off Duty, on a win or a loss)
- Popping is a craft and you are a craftsman. (Enemies Defeated, on a win)
- That sound never gets less alarming. (Enemies Defeated, on a loss)
- Accuracy like that is wasted on a weapon like that. (Bombs On Target, on a win or a loss)
- You are a marksman. Of the worst possible discipline. (Bombs On Target, on a win or a loss)
- Not one wasted. Somebody at home is very proud and very confused. (Bombs On Target, on a win)
- Direct deposit. Straight to the top floor. (Direct Deposit, on a win or a loss)
- Right on the head. That is going to be very hard to explain. (Direct Deposit, on a win or a loss)
- Precision bombing. Genuinely disgusting. Well done. (Direct Deposit, on a win)
- Back to back to back. No breaks. No shame. (In One Sitting, on a win or a loss)
- That is a streak. An unbroken, unwelcome streak. (In One Sitting, on a win or a loss)
- You found a rhythm. Everyone wishes you hadn't. (In One Sitting, on a win)
- There is more of it on the level than in you at this point. (Longest Streak Of Poo, on a win or a loss)
- Volume like that raises real medical questions. (Longest Streak Of Poo, on a win or a loss)
- You took a lot of that. Most of it personally. (Received, on a loss)
- Caught more than you threw. That is a losing ratio in any sport. (Received, on a win or a loss)
- You went out wearing most of the level. (Received, on a loss)
- Everybody got some. Nobody was spared. Democratic. (Full Coverage, on a win)
- Full coverage. Not one of them left clean. (Full Coverage, on a win)
- You died filthy. That is how they will remember you. (Died Dirty, on a loss)
- Covered in it AND dead. A comprehensive defeat. (Died Dirty, on a loss)
- Went down absolutely caked. No dignity in the final frame. (Died Dirty, on a loss)
